items.summary: Abstract Electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) offers a sustainable route for converting CO2 into value-added chemicals and fuels, yet its practical application is hindered by CO2 transport limitations and salt precipitation in membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzers. items.summary: This study investigates the profound impact of residual solvents and thermal history on the CO 2 /CH 4 and CO 2 /N 2 separation performance of 6FDA-based polyimide membranes by providing a comprehensive understanding of how solvent-polymer-penetrant interactions dictate macroscopic separation efficiency. items.summary: Efficient CO 2 transport design is essential for early-stage carbon capture and storage (CCS) studies, yet detailed pipeline optimization is difficult to repeatedly embed in CCS chain assessments with varying CO 2 quality and economic assumptions. items.summary: CO2-enhanced coalbed methane recovery (CO2-ECBM) is a vital approach for synergizing deep methane extraction with geological carbon storage. items.authors: Tiancong Ding, Chong Sun, Ruiyan Li, Xueqiang Lin, Jianbo Sun
items.summary: In this study, a mutual solubility model for CO 2 transport systems containing multiple impurities (CH 4 , N 2 , H 2 , CO, Ar, O 2 , H 2 S and SO 2 ) is established. items.authors: Altti Meriläinen, Antti Kosonen, Peter Holtappels, Roland Dittmeyer, Pertti Kauranen, Jero Ahola
items.summary: Reducing the atmospheric CO 2 concentration to a sustainable level requires large-scale carbon dioxide removal through direct air capture (DAC). DAC is a heat-intensive process, and waste heat recovery to supply its heat demand has substantial potential to reduce the levelized cost of DAC (LCODAC). This study determines the techno-economic potential of recovering low-temperature waste heat (70°C) from an off-grid electrolyzer plant for use in a solid-sorbent DAC plant requiring heat at 80°C–120°C for desorption. items.authors: Emma Coatney, May L. Martin, Kip O. Findley, Lawrence Cho
items.summary: Carbon steel pipelines are widely used for CO2 transport in carbon capture, utilization, and storage applications.
